body: these references are no longer stable now I think
what do you mean by no longer stable? could you explain more?
if you do addEventListener on an early render, the function reference isn't the same as another one, meaning that removeEventListener wouldn't work I think (although I always get confused about this)
Understood, that's very error prone. I updated the tests to check that we get the same function at the first and second renders.
this can be two separate tests if the second uses `getInitializedWidget`
same here, one test for init, one for render will be clearer if we ever break anything on it
the cache read is still here, but not the cache write, is that expected?
the cache read should probably move from render to before here, wdyt?

maybe we can expose it from getWidgetRenderState as well, something like "currentPage", to use for sendEvent?

It makes sense not to compute the cache read multiple times

I don't really see the advantage of doing this, we will still have 2 renders to do in the second test anyway. Also since there is a relation between the 2 renders (the functions we got from the second render must match the ones we received in the first), I think it is clearer to keep everything in the same test.

It is expected, we need it for the `sendEvent` call that must stay in `render`.
One alternative way I thought of was to return `cachedHits` from `getWidgetRenderState` but I don't know if it is better or not.

I did not understood what you meant by that, can you explain more precisely?

(all this side effects like update of the `results` object and `cache.write` should not be in `getWidgetRenderState` which should be a pure getter but I did not wanted to mess with the logic here for now)

As @Haroenv and @francoischalifour discussed in another PR, when we get rid of `init` in the future, it's natural that `getWidgetRenderState` is the place where side effects occur.

Although `getWidgetRenderState` has side effects, I think it's okay as long as it's idempotent. In this case, it's okay to call `getWidgetRenderState` multiple times as long as it reads the cache and writes the same one (not changing the cache). And, of course, `getWidgetRenderState` shouldn't trigger `sendEvent` inside it.

To sum up, I think it's good to have `cache.read` inside `getWidgetRenderState`. And we add another property to `InfiniteHitsWidgetRenderState`, which is something like `currentPageHits`. If so, inside `render` we can get `currentPageHits` from the render state and call `sendEvent`.

What do you think?
We'd better make this `[]` by default, or to make the type optional, because `getWidgetRenderState` here returns `undefind` as `currentPageHits` when there's no results.
